title: To Thee, My God! to Thee I Bring
description: To Thee, My God! to Thee I Bring in Tonic Solfa to SELENA, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: John Bowring wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 963 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Evening Hymn with Nature”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SELENA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: To Thee, my God! to thee I bring The e-vening's grate-ful of-fe-ring; From thee, the source of joy a-bove, Flow ev-er-last-ing streams of love; And all the rays of light that shine, And bless cre-a-tion, Lord! are thine.

lines: To Thee, my God! to thee I bring
The evening's grateful offering;
From thee, the source of joy above,
Flow everlasting streams of love;
And all the rays of light that shine,
And bless creation, Lord! are thine.
The morn, when stepping down the hills —
The noon, which all creation fills
With glory; evening's placid fall,
The twilight and the raven pall
Of midnight; all alike proclaim
Thy great, thine all impressive name.
And from the little worm, whose light
Shines palely through the shades of night,
Up to the sparkling stars that run
Their evening rounds — or glorious sun,
Rolling his car to twilight's rest —
All, all in thee is bright and blest.
And over all — above, below,
We see thee — ever-present thou!
In every wandering rill that flows,
In every gentle breeze that blows;
In every rising, setting sun,
We trace thee — own thee — holy One!
Yes! in the mid-day's fervid beams,
And in the midnight's shadowy dreams,
In action and repose, we see,
We recognize and worship thee;
To thee our worthiest songs would give,
And in thee die, and to thee live.

licence: Public domain: John Bowring died in 1872.
credits: Words by John Bowring (1792–1872), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SELENA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
